top_level_objectives: Represent physical quantities with vectors and interpret magnitude and direction in 2D.
Add vectors tip-to-tail and resolve a vector into perpendicular components using trigonometry.
Apply vector components to explain two-dimensional projectile motion.
Predict how launch angle and speed affect range, maximum height, and trajectory shape.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 1: Introducing vectors as directed quantities
scenes.brief_purpose: Establish the idea that some physical quantities need both size and direction, and motivate vectors as a compact representation.
key_visuals: A 2D coordinate plane with several arrows of different lengths and orientations.
Labels showing magnitude and direction next to arrows.
A simple comparison between scalar quantities and vector quantities.
student_actions: Inspect the arrows and identify which features represent magnitude and which represent direction.
Select example quantities and decide whether each should be treated as a scalar or a vector.
Rotate or compare arrows to see how changing direction changes the vector even when length stays the same.

scenes.brief_purpose: Build intuition for vector addition by showing how two vectors combine into a single resultant.
key_visuals: Two arrows arranged head-to-tail on a grid.
A resultant arrow drawn from the starting point of the first vector to the ending point of the second.
A changing resultant as the student varies the second vector.
student_actions: Place one vector after another and observe the resultant that connects start to finish.
Predict the resultant direction and size before revealing it.
Compare different vector pairs to see how addition depends on both magnitude and direction.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 3: Breaking a vector into components
scenes.brief_purpose: Show that one vector can be represented by perpendicular x and y components, linking geometry to physical interpretation.
key_visuals: A vector at an angle to horizontal axes.
Perpendicular component arrows forming a right triangle.
Angle and side-length labels that connect the vector to its components.
student_actions: Choose an axis system and decompose the vector into horizontal and vertical parts.
Use the right triangle to relate the vector’s magnitude and angle to its components.
Change the vector angle and observe how the component sizes shift.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 4: Connecting components to motion in a projectile launch
scenes.brief_purpose: Apply vector decomposition to the initial velocity of a launched projectile and introduce independent horizontal and vertical motion.
key_visuals: A projectile launched from a platform at an angle.
An initial velocity vector split into horizontal and vertical components.
Separate visual tracks for horizontal motion and vertical motion.
student_actions: Set a launch angle and speed, then identify the initial velocity components.
Observe that the horizontal component stays steady while the vertical component changes under gravity.
Explain, using the visuals, why the motion can be analyzed separately in x and y.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 5: Following the full trajectory under gravity
scenes.brief_purpose: Show how constant horizontal velocity and changing vertical velocity combine to produce a parabolic path.
key_visuals: A projectile following a curved arc across a field.
A sequence of position markers showing equal-time motion.
Vectors indicating horizontal motion remains uniform while vertical motion changes during ascent and descent.
student_actions: Watch the projectile move and connect the path to its component motions.
Identify the highest point and note the change in vertical motion there.
Relate the shape of the trajectory to the combination of independent horizontal and vertical behavior.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 6: Exploring launch angle and speed
scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate the concepts by having students vary launch conditions and observe effects on range and maximum height.
key_visuals: Multiple trajectories overlaid for different launch angles and speeds.
A range marker on the ground and a height indicator near the peak.
Side-by-side comparisons of shallow, moderate, and steep launches.
student_actions: Adjust launch angle and speed to compare different trajectories.
Predict which setting gives the greatest range or highest peak, then test it.
Summarize how changing initial velocity components alters the outcome of the motion.
